label: Late copy steps of short (L=3/4) sequences, esp. last output of L=3
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original tokens or on <DEL>), and only when the input token is a repeat (in_first=0). It is concentrated in very short sequences: L=3 has a 10% active rate (63% of mass) and L=4 a 0.8% rate (21% of mass). The peak is the final copy step of L=3 sequences (t=5, recall_idx=2, input = orig(1)), which holds 54% of mass. Smaller pockets: recall_idx 1 in L=3 (t=4), recall_idx 2-3 in L=4 (t=6-7), and t=12 in L=9. The identity of the fed-back input token strongly modulates both firing and magnitude: f, t and p give the top activations (f is ~1.0 of max), while digits and letters like g, n, e and l rarely fire even at the peak position. Precision is limited because most L=3 last steps with other input tokens do not fire. A positional description alone (L=3, recall_idx=2) gets dev F1 0.42 (P 0.48, R 0.38, mass recall 0.54). Broadening to all late copy steps of L<=4 raises mass recall to 0.83 but drops precision to 0.13.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=6: f, t, p, o; t=12: t, f, p, o; t=4: f, t, p, j) and the previous input (most: j, c, y, 2, r, 3; least: x, o, v, m); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=5, L=4 & t=6.
